title: Ericsson and Partners Launch Sferical One AI Supercomputer in Sweden
source_used: Tech Times (16 Oct 2026) and NVIDIA blog (15 Oct 2026)
key_facts: Sferical One, a supercomputer jointly owned by AstraZeneca, Ericsson, Saab, SEB and Wallenberg Investments, was formally launched in Stockholm on 15 Oct 2026, with Nvidia's Jensen Huang on stage.
It runs two NVIDIA DGX SuperPODs with 1,152 Blackwell Ultra GPUs in 16 DGX GB300 NVL72 racks (Tech Times and NVIDIA's blog agree).
It has been running since late summer 2026, per Tech Times.
Tech Times says the aim is to run frontier-scale AI on sensitive proprietary data without routing it through a US-based cloud.
The partners buy compute capacity at per-GPU-hour rates from Sferical AI, which operates the cluster; Sferical AI was formed in August 2025.
It uses NVIDIA Nemotron open-weights models; a dedicated NVIDIA AI Technology Centre in Sweden is planned.
NVIDIA's blog (15 Oct 2026) names SKF as strategic partner.
quote_evidence: The machine is called Sferical One. It has been running since late summer 2026.
Sferical One is built on two NVIDIA DGX SuperPODs, spanning 1,152 Blackwell Ultra GPUs organized across 16 NVIDIA DGX GB300 NVL72 systems.

In Sweden, a consortium anchored by Ericsson, AstraZeneca, Saab, SEB and Wallenberg Investments, with SKF as strategic partner, launched Sferical One — a shared supercomputer running on two NVIDIA DGX SuperPODs with 16 racks of NVIDIA DGX GB300 systems and 1,152 GPUs.
why_it_matters_hint: Large European companies pooling money for their own AI computing to keep sensitive data in Sweden.
notes: Pool source HPCwire (an Ericsson press release, Cloudflare block) not readable; Tech Times (analysis-heavy) and NVIDIA's blog read. Event is 15 Oct 2026, older than the window. Tech Times names Per Narvinger as Ericsson CEO; not used because it is single-source.
